answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.6.2024) The fight against drug trafficking is a priority of the Commission as highlighted in the EU Roadmap to fight drug trafficking and organised crime1.

On 28 November 2023, the Commission presented legislative proposals to strengthen the fight against migrant smuggling networks2 and launched the Global Alliance to Counter Migrant Smuggling3, calling for stronger international cooperation to limit the supply of smuggling-relevant equipment, including boats.

From a technical aspect, small rigid inflatable boats and their engines intended for recreational purposes are subject to Recreational Craft Directive4 which does not limit the maximum power of engines. However, Article 5 of the Directive enables Member States to restrict the navigation on certain waters to ensure safety.

Small boats not intended for recreational purposes must fulfil the general safety requirements embedded in the General Products Safety Directive5. There are currently no specific provisions at EU level concerning use of boats for criminal purposes.
1 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council on the EU roadmap to fight

drug trafficking and organised crime, COM/2023/641 final. 2 COM(2023)754 final and COM(2023)755 final. Article 6(5)(f) and Article 8(2)(i) of COM(2023)754 final indicate that penalties for natural persons and for legal persons respectively include the freezing and confiscation of the proceeds derived from, and instrumentalities used for, the commission of the offence of migrant smuggling.

Recital 17 clarifies that this applies to boats, engines and other boat components and vehicles. For this purpose, full use should be made of existing instruments on the freezing and confiscation of proceeds and instrumentalities of crime, such as Directive 2014/42/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council. 3 https://ec.europa.
